Notes from the wave-2 boundary: contract change requests forwarded to this work package, with the lead's decisions. The architecture and wps.json already reflect the decisions; these notes give detail.
- [CR 63 from WP-11] accesslog.Writer.Acquire returns a record whose FailureModes is nil. Submit copies the entries and never keeps the slice, and the record is zeroed when it returns to the pool. The access-record feed (WP-43) or the handler (WP-66) should assign its own reused per-request []emit.FailureModeEntry (at most 8 entries) instead of appending to the nil field, which keeps records with failure modes at zero allocations in steady state. Strings in the record must still be immutable values, never views of pooled buffers (emit.AccessRecord doc).
- [CR 28 from WP-06] WP-43: on the client view, Exchange.SetIdentity(id) refuses a second binding with filter.ErrSecondBinding. Otherwise it must fill the CEL activation: Vars.Auth = &expr.Auth{Method: id.Method, Claims: id.Claims}, Vars.Consumer = id.Consumer (nil, so CEL null, when unbound) and, for auth.mtls, Vars.Source.ClientCertSubject = id.CertSubject (the expr.Source doc comment). If Vars is already populated for the current Phase (a `when` evaluated before the auth Policy ran), update it at once, so later Policies' `when` and CEL in the same Phase see the identity. Leg Vars copies taken afterwards inherit it. Before authentication, and on Routes without an auth-class Policy, Auth and Consumer stay nil (spec 06 req 4). id.Claims may be an expr.Value implemented outside internal/cel (auth.EmptyClaims(), whose Native() is an empty map): store it as is, without conversion. celtypes already accepts foreign Values through Native() (celtypes.ToVal in internal/cel/celtypes/value.go, test "claims from a foreign Value" in value_test.go), so the WP-08 half of this note is done.
extra.WP-47:
Notes from the wave-2 boundary: contract change requests forwarded to this work package, with the lead's decisions. The architecture and wps.json already reflect the decisions; these notes give detail.
- [CR 7 from WP-02] An *Object with more than 8 members keeps a name index that Decode, Clone and every mutation maintain. Decode charges CostIndexEntry (48) per member for that index, so for large objects the *Object form costs more than Options.MapObjects (map[string]any); budgets and reservations must use the cost Decode returns for the form you actually build. Reads (Len, At, All, Index, Get, Has) never write, so one decoded tree may be shared read-only by any number of goroutines (the shared decoded body of 03 req 25 and 07 req 56). Any mutation (Set, SetAt, Delete, DeleteAt, Sort, transforms, merge) needs exclusive access, so call Clone (jsonval.Clone or Object.Clone) before editing a shared tree. MaxCostPerByte (33) bounds cost per input byte; the oversize budget multiple is the one recorded in 2.16 for request 5 (4 times the raw limit).
- [CR 9 from WP-20] No SPI change is needed. WP-06 (committed) already defines the documented auth.Challenger in internal/filter/auth/auth.go:69-77, and *auth.Decider implements Challenge() (decider.go:63). The executor asserts an identical executor.Challenger on p.Filter (run.go:195) for the 401 RZ-AUTH-001 of Security rule 1. Note for WP-47, WP-48 and WP-49: the Filter value your Factory returns MUST have its own `Challenge() string` method. Get it by embedding *auth.Decider anonymously (promoted method) or by forwarding to it. A Decider held in a named field is invisible to the executor's type assertion, and the 401 then carries no WWW-Authenticate. Build the Decider with auth.NewAuth(m, challenge): auth.jwt uses auth.ChallengeJWT, auth.api-key uses auth.APIKeyChallenge(auth.APIKeyHeader(cfg.Header)), auth.basic uses auth.ChallengeBasic, and auth.mtls uses "" (no challenge, a documented deviation). Add a unit test per type asserting that p.Filter.(interface{ Challenge() string }) succeeds with the expected value.
- [CR 29 from WP-06] WP-70: give every snapshot compile its own filter.BuildEnv.Shared. It is a concurrency-safe, single-flight memo shared by all W workers of that compile and dropped afterwards. Build snapshot.Consumers and every BuildEnv.Consumers from one identity.CompileBundle(validated.Bundle).Map(), so the identity.Index from auth.AcquireIndex returns the same *expr.Consumer pointers the snapshot holds. On a failed or abandoned compile, Close (filter.Closer) every Filter already built so its index reference is released; otherwise a KeyIndex keeps its secret watches, or a later acquirer gets auth.ErrIndexClosed. WP-47/48/49 (auth.jwt, auth.api-key, auth.basic, auth.mtls): call auth.AcquireIndex(env) in Build, including when reusing env.Previous, because Consumers can change without the Policy changing. Each must implement auth.IndexHolder (`CredentialIndex() *identity.Index`, returning the held index) so the next compile carries the KeyIndex over (R-55), and call Index.Release() exactly once from Close.

- [CR 144 from WP-28] The rendered schema's $defs/JSONSchemaDocument (validation.json-schema config.schema: type [object, boolean], no properties) is opaque. Detect it through schemaidx: its Node has Def() == "JSONSchemaDocument" (Def follows the $ref), and every position below it is Info.Free with a nil Node. WP-36 overlay: an overlay value at that node replaces the base value whole and never merges recursively (docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md Overlays table, 'Replaced whole as one atomic value'; 07 req 74). WP-36 subst: string scalars inside are substituted like any other free string (a literal ${ is written $${) and are never re-typed. WP-37: normalize its object keys generically (02 req 18), materialize no defaults inside it, and keep every list inside in authored order (schemaidx ListNone is atomic, 02 req 17). Add tests: an overlay that changes one keyword replaces the whole document, and normalization keeps the order of `enum` and `required`.
- [CR 161 from WP-29] config/overlay treats the value at any position whose schema node is the `JSONSchemaDocument` definition (`validation.json-schema` `config.schema`) as one atomic value: an overlay value replaces it whole and nothing inside it is merged (CM Overlays table row 'Value of the schema's JSONSchemaDocument definition'; 07 req 74). Detect it by definition name through schemaidx: `info.Node.Def() == "JSONSchemaDocument"`, where Node.Def returns the nearest $defs name. No new x-ruralz schema marker is added, because the CM keyword table defines five and the lead does not invent one, so WP-28 and WP-29 need no change. Add an overlay test in which the base and overlay schemas share keys and the result equals the overlay's schema exactly.

- [CR 20 from WP-04] Callers of registry.Registry.Phases (WP-38 precedence, WP-56 validate, WP-59 authz.cel Factory) and WP-69, which injects the oracle into precedence, must follow two rules. First, Phases fails with registry.ErrNoBodyOracle when an authz.cel Policy has a non-empty config.rule and the BodyOracle argument is nil. Pass the CEL compiler, the expr.Compiler value that internal/cel implements, which has ReferencesRequestBody, on every Phases call that can see authz.cel, and never nil in a binary. Second, Phases rejects an Attachment.Config whose type is not the Policy type's config type, for every type and before the scope rule. Pass hub.Resource.Config exactly as stage G decoded it (the registry's NewConfig pointer type, such as *v1alpha1.AuthzCELConfig), or nil.
extra.WP-44:
Notes from the wave-2 boundary: contract change requests forwarded to this work package, with the lead's decisions. The architecture and wps.json already reflect the decisions; these notes give detail.
- [CR 85 from WP-16] Lead decision: the tlsconf row of 1.2 stays 'secret, errcode' (no v1alpha1), so the v1alpha1-typed signatures that spec 06 section 3 sketches are not built. Listener certificates become `[]tlsconf.CertSpec{Name, Certificate: secret.RefOf(c.Certificate), PrivateKey: secret.RefOf(c.PrivateKey)}` for `tlsconf.BuildCertIndex(specs, store)`, then `tlsconf.NewListenerState(tlsconf.ListenerOptions{MinVersion, Certs, RequestClientCert})`; the snapshot compiler does this conversion. Upstream.spec.tls and telemetry.otlp.tls become `tlsconf.ClientSpec{SNI, CACertificate, ClientCertificate, ClientKey *secret.Ref}` for `tlsconf.Upstream(spec, store)` and `tlsconf.OTLP(&spec, store)` (nil spec: system roots). The owner calls Close on the CertIndex or ClientConfig when it retires it, which stops its secret watches.
- [CR 89 from WP-16] tlsconf.ServerOptions has only State, and the tlsconf.Server configuration does not observe handshakes: crypto/tls has no post-handshake hook, and VerifyConnection runs before the client's last flight. Measure spec 06 req 77 around the listener's own (*tls.Conn).HandshakeContext call: a nil error observes ruralz_listener_tls_handshake_duration_seconds from accept, and an error counts ruralz_listener_connections_total{result='tls_failure'}. On the Go 1.26 floor, net/http handshakes a *tls.Conn itself with no completion hook, so complete the handshake (bounded by the listener's handshake timeout) before handing the *tls.Conn to http.Server, which then skips its own. Do this per connection off the Accept loop, on goroutines the listener owns and bounds by the connection ceiling, so a slow client cannot stall accepts. Build tls.Server over the connection wrapper that implements tlsconf.ClientCertRecorder, so GetConfigForClient can record the request mode on the NetConn chain.
- [CR 4 from WP-15] clientaddr.ListenerOptions.Clock must track wall time, because Clock.Now()+Timeout goes to net.Conn.SetReadDeadline, which the OS enforces against the real clock. A fake seeded at a fixed date refuses every PROXY connection at once, or never times out. Production passes clock.Real() (WP-76 wiring); tests pass clock.Real() or clocktest.New(clock.Real().Now()). The gateway/listener row in 1.2 does not list clock, so take a clientaddr.TimeSource (clock.Clock satisfies it) through the listener's options instead of importing clock.

extra.WP-54:
Notes from the wave-2 boundary: contract change requests forwarded to this work package, with the lead's decisions. The architecture and wps.json already reflect the decisions; these notes give detail.
- [CR 132 from WP-27] make release-dry-run (WP-27, fixed by 4.1 rule 3) runs from the repo root. Step 1 removes dist/release, then runs `go run ./internal/tool/releasekit package -dist dist -out dist/release -version V -commit C`, which writes the archives, dist/notices/<bin>_<os>_<arch>/ for the Dockerfile (recreate it on every run; only dist/release is removed), the schema assets and release-manifest.json. Step 2 runs Syft itself (`syft scan file:<archive> -o cyclonedx-json@1.7=<archive>.cdx.json` for each .tar.gz and .zip). Step 3 runs `releasekit checksums -dir dist/release`, then `releasekit notes -from <previous v* tag, or the literal root> -to HEAD -budgets dist/bench -skipped <FILE or ''> -out dist/release/NOTES.md` (an empty -skipped means no skipped gates), then `releasekit verify -manifest dist/release/release-manifest.json`, and finally `cd dist/release && sha256sum -c --quiet SHA256SUMS`, so SHA256SUMS must be GNU format with names relative to dist/release; the .cdx.json files already exist when checksums runs, so decide and document whether they are listed. make release then runs `cosign sign-blob --yes --bundle dist/release/SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json dist/release/SHA256SUMS`, so releasekit never signs, never runs Syft and never runs sha256sum. Exit 1 on findings and 2 on usage or I/O errors (tools-ci convention); the target skips packaging while internal/tool/releasekit has no .go files.
- [CR 138 from WP-27] When `releasekit package` runs, dist/<os>_<arch>/ holds three binaries. ruralzd is there for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 (production) and for darwin/arm64 and darwin/amd64 (development-only archives built by release-dry-run, not by stage 4). ruralz is there for linux/{amd64,arm64}, darwin/{arm64,amd64} and windows/amd64 (ruralz.exe, archived as .zip). ruralz-control is there for linux/{amd64,arm64}; it is the M2 stub and package must not archive it (11 req 91: no ruralz-control archive until M2). dist/ also holds non-platform directories (dist/bench, dist/fuzz, dist/notices and the -out directory dist/release itself), so package reads only directories named <os>_<arch> and fails when an expected binary is missing instead of skipping it. Add a test over a fake dist tree that contains those extra directories and the ruralz-control binaries.
extra.WP-65:
Notes from the wave-2 boundary: contract change requests forwarded to this work package, with the lead's decisions. The architecture and wps.json already reflect the decisions; these notes give detail.
- [CR 78 from WP-14] In gateway.Run(ctx, args, stdout, stderr), call `setting.Load(args, os.LookupEnv)` with the args cmd/ruralzd passes (os.Args[1:]; Run never reads os.Args itself). On error, write the error and `setting.Usage` to stderr and return `setting.ExitCode(err)`, which is 2 for a *setting.Error and 1 otherwise. Log each name in `Settings.Unused` at warn as unused in file mode. Build the egress guard with `egress.ParseAllow(s.FetchAllow)` (not egress.FromEnv, so the environment is read once), and create the secret resolver with `resolver.Config{Root: s.SecretRoot, Protected: ...}`, converting each `setting.ProtectedPath{Setting, Path}` from `s.Protected()` into a `resolver.Protected{Setting, Path}`. Pass `s.MACKey.Bytes()` (a copy; nil when unset) to the State Store manager: WP-65 accepts that []byte and puts it in `statestore.Deps.MACKey` for every driver it opens (R-49). Never log the key; MACKey's text forms print [REDACTED].
- [CR 146 from WP-28] WP-28 fixed Gateway.spec.stateStore.cache as $defs/StateStoreCache = {topology (StateStoreTopology, default standalone), url (required SecretValue, x-ruralz-secret, impact security)}. It has no driver field and no timeout field. WP-65: when cache is set, open the RoleCache driver with statestore.Config{Role: RoleCache, Driver: DriverRedis (always), Topology from cache.topology, URL = resolved cache.url, DefaultTimeout = the main stateStore.timeout (default 50ms), Source: SourceGateway}. RURALZ_STATE_STORE_URL and the memory fallback apply to the main role only. When cache is absent, the cache shares the main handle under the interim rules and logs the startup WARN (R-19). cache.url's secret destination is state-store (R-49), so its dialer dials only that URL's host. WP-70: a cache Policy's effective stateStoreTimeout (BuildEnv.StateStoreTimeout) defaults to the main stateStore.timeout even when stateStore.cache is set, and BuildEnv.CacheStore is the RoleCache handle when present, else the main handle.
